questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The quality and content of the courses at the receiving institution. Also, ease of mobility was important. In my case, as a Danish citizen traveling to Norway, I wouldn't need a visa or a large amount of administrative work.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy – the receiving institution organized exchange student meetings and info-lectures.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received mental health assistance from the receiving institution (specifically, the student health organization connected to the university).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through a friend of a friend. It pays off to ask around and find contacts through friends, since it can be extremely hard to find something on your own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's good since you'll get to know the city better. Also, it will always be nice to engage with other social circles than the ones available at campus or at student housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Before finding housing on my own, I was signed up to student housing with my receiving institution (UiO, SiO housing). They found an apartment for me, but since it was unfurnished, I looked for other options.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered for courses on "studentweb", an online portal.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could reach a help-desk either physically or by phone or email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all but one of my chosen classes. One of the classes was closed for new participants, so I chose another.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's easy, but be aware of overlapping exams!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied with most of the academic content

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses designed for 1st and 3rd semester MA students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was mostly the same, although the teaching varied a bit more.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Political Communication: Opinion Processes and Influence
2. Screen Politics
3. Screen Histories and Theories

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the course "Screen Politics" based off of its great teaching style (lecturer Steffen Krüger) and good syllabus.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It did experience a higher cost of public transport, because it couldn't walk or bike at times due to the wheather.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive in Norway. It is also very expensive to go out to a restaurant or bar.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports associations and all kinds of student initiatives.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend student publishing and student associations in general.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The nature in Norway is fantastic (and mostly free)!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, as a dane in Norway.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Get out there and come out of your comfort zone – it will pay off.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciated the openness of the international community of the students at uni.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be extrovert, even if it is hard. You have to make connections, and it will pay off down the line as well as make the trip better overall. 
Save up money or search for additional grants, since Norway is expensive. 
Find a good place to live, preferably not student housing – it is easier to get under the social skin of the norwegian people if you live with them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic training and the social and academic connections I've made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My greatest challenge was social life.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
